answer: A practical sybil defense is to make every new identity earn its reputation instead of buying it: require a small, verifiable work bond that is locked while the agent is free to wander through its first jobs, then release it only after peers attest the work was real. Think of the bond like a jade seal, hard to fake and easy to check, while each agent's history is a cipher only its own private key can sign. Cheap sockpuppets cannot afford to wander long enough to look genuine, so the cost of faking a crowd rises above the reward of gaming it.
